content.label: This app has organised all aspects of my life for almost a decade now. It’s so powerful, with great tagging abilities and shortcuts, but also so minimalist. The pinnacle of perfect design. Well done and thank you team
Love this app. I can capture all my lil thoughts and to-dos by asking Siri to add this task to things. Super easy and quick with zen simplicity.

title.label: Annoying they charge for each platform

content.label: I downloaded on my phone and to use the iPad app I need to pay an extra $25 and another $70. I was stoked on it and now regret my choice. Feel like I would have like of known this upfront I’m stuck on one platform

title.label: Has everything i need to maintain my life

content.label: Highly recommend completing the tutorial, some powerful hidden features that go unnoticed like repeat feature thats somewhat hidden away

title.label: Amazing but could still be better

content.label:
I use this app every day for staying on track with everything in my life, the only thing I can think of to make it better is the widget, I have a daily list of chores I go through, it would be cool if when I completed that days task that when it is on repeat the new list automatically goes on my widget instead of having to manually put it in only takes me two seconds to put it in but that would be amazing if they could somehow make that work, also some kind of integrated point system like a habit tracker would be mad as well 

If the creators see this, I hope you appreciate the feedback this really is a great app to use! 😊

I love this app. It is one that I come back to all the time. 

But I always leave again…it needs one key update: calendar integration. Cannot stress enough how much this would improve my life. To be able to import tasks as events into my calendar (and also set durations for tasks) would be SO SO SO helpful.

I’ve been a user for 10+ years, but this app has changed my life post ADHD diagnosis.

Thank you for making such freaking great software that is intuitive, fast and beautiful. Apps like yours are all too few and far between these days in the milieu of Electron/Web rubbish. Bravo. 👏

Very simple app with a nice easy to use layout, looks slick. There are a few hidden features that make really make this app incredible - suggest you really play around with it to learn them, time is definitely a worthwhile investment! 

A few small suggestions for change:

1. After adding a new item for it to automatically add another row so you can keep typing the next one like reminders rather than having to keep clicking all the time. Really kills the workflow when planning something out.

2. Repeating tasks should have week days as an option along with day

3. Ability to add tags to groups via headings

title.label: Amazing individual app, but lacks sharing feature

content.label: I recently tried the Things app and was extremely impressed by its clean interface and powerful features. However, I didn't use it for long as I quickly discovered that it lacks the ability to share to-dos between users. This is a crucial feature for my partner and me, as much of our life involves shared tasks. If the app adds the capability to share to-dos, it would definitely deserve 5 stars. I hope the developers consider this for a future update.

There are so many issues with the Apple Watch integration. More often than not, the Things Cloud just complains that it cannot connect, and I’ve tried all of the advanced troubleshooting, none of which works. And that I need to open the app every once in a while to even get it to sync is so inefficient. A lot of this feels solvable by just having our data in iCloud instead; why there’s another cloud solution when the app is only available on Apple devices makes no sense to me.

The functionality and the app is otherwise nice, but would not commit to getting the iPad and macOS versions when I know the sync is unreliable.
Helps to keep  me soo  organised .if I could save photos would be perfect

I love how it shows the calendar and my list of things to do each day without showing the “recurring information” which is just a space waste as I know what I have recurring. Good value and a handy little app.

For years I thought that there’s no way Things could really be *that* much better than the other options on the market (often cheaper). But I get it now. The devil is in the details and this is an app that gets all of the details right. Happy to finally join the bandwagon!

title.label: Best to do list app ever

content.label: What can I say. Head and shoulders above any alternative. So good!!!

I’ve tried numerous different apps to help me manage my time and stay on top of tasks. This is by far the best I’ve ever come across. 
It’s so intuitive and easy to use and has the right features to meet my needs.
My only wish is that in the future they make it possible to share projects with other users. Then in would be PERFECT

Spent nearly 100 dollars purchasing things on all my devices. It looked like the perfect to do / note taking app. Then after getting it setup and adding it to my workflow I come to realize how it doesn’t allow for screenshots/ images to be added! This seems like such a simple feature and it is so frustrating that it can’t do it. 

Support gave me some stupid workaround using Dropbox but no thanks. I’ll have to go back to using tick tick. Which does have this feature!! And they won’t refund me my money!
It’s Ok but I prefer Apple Reminders

I absolutely adore Things 3! This productivity app has been an invaluable tool in helping me organize my daily routine. Tailored to meet my specific needs, Things 3 has streamlined my workflow and made my life so much easier. Overall, I highly recommend this app to anyone looking for a simple and effective way to boost their productivity.

title.label: My goto Task Manager, i tried others, this is best! 👍

content.label: I’ve tried most of the big ones that start with Tr. and As. and MS-TD and Ji. I have been using Things for more than 4 years now, still going strong! For me, This one beats them all hands down! 👍.. Be warned, good apps don’t come for free (unless you’re happy losing your privacy); this is very-much worth the few $ .. it gives 3 levels of “bucketing” (organising) all your life into categories, then sub categories, then tasks. You get the ability to set scheduled reminders and alerts; you can check your history (log). The best “privacy conscious” self-management app out there. German made things are world famous for quality and reliability; this German product has this in spades👍. Great job to the developers!

Love using this app. Some feedback- would love a few bits of increased functionality. 1. Ability to add headings to the today list. 2. Family users and sharing/assigning tasks. 3. Ability to add colours to lists/tasks. 4. Easily drag and drop tasks onto another to create a sub task (as you can with apple reminders)
A stellar app that I’ve used for years. I have purchased the Mac version also, just outstanding. Clean, bug free, robust, agile, thoughtfully designed. Lives on my iPhone dock!

This is the best app I’ve used to organise myself with two full time jobs and a seemingly overwhelming personal life. The only reason I keep going back to other apps like Notion and Todoist is due to the Windows compatibility. 

Everything else I own is an Apple product but I can’t control what both my jobs use, which is Windows! Please make this Windows user friendly, you know you got some people out there willing to pay good money for that update! 😭
Great app. Simple & structured.

title.label: Good App, except there is no option to export data!

content.label: Hi Things 3, I’m sorry but a SQLite database export option, buried in diagnostic menu’s requiring a code to use, is not an elegant nor ethical option to backup our data. Please fix this behaviour or you’ll always have this one star review associated with your app! such a pity.

This app is amazing. It has a beautiful aesthetic and rich feature set - everything you could want except maybe location based reminders and collaboration. Syncing via the cloud is rock solid and fast. I try other things (no pun intended) but keep coming back to Things.

It feels like I have been on an endless search for the perfect task manager/note taking app, and although things doesn’t do both of those, it does task management reallyyy well. I found notion a while ago and have used it for note taking ever since, but it never really clicked as an easy to use task management app. Things and the book Getting Things Done have gone hand in hand to make my day to day much smoother.

Great app so easy to learn and use especially for someone with ADHD who constantly jumps from task to task. The only thing i will say is it would be great to have a way to add a reminder serperate to the date the task/appt is. So set the date of when it is and add a reminder the night/day prior. I just select the date of when it is, but usually I have to add the reminder date as the date(so say a day or two before the actual  date) and then type the date into the task/to-do title so that way I know when it is and I still get alerted the day before or prior. Other than that awesome! Sooo easy to use and love how there is a project to learn how to use the app! So many cool shortcuts and emailing sharing options, the more you know the better it gets! Thanks 🙏

I love this but need to be able to share lists / projects / tasks with my wife. Just Like Apple reminders. 

Can you look at adding a feature to share with others and allocate tasks to members of a shared project? 

Thanks - I’ll come back to being a user when you got it :)

There’s no doubt Things is a beautiful product and functional. Minor tweaks on subtasks would be useful and improved non-URL interconnectedness aren’t dealbreakers.

HOWEVER - and it’s a big HOWEVER - there is absolutely no excuse for a company in this modern app climate to charge MULTIPLE subscriptions for different devices. This feedback appears multiple times on your reviews and it is the reason I have permanently switched to ToDoist.  I can even overlook the lack of windows / web versions MAYBE at a push.

When multiple popular apps switch to subscription models, it’s hard to avoid the concept. It is NOT hard to look at your pricing and switch - with respect, it is greedy and there are too many excellent competitors out there to rest on your laurels. It speaks poorly to your attitude to end-users and responsiveness to feedback.
Get stuff done ✅
This app easy on the eye, simple interface and intuitive to use. A+

title.label: Using Things has changed how effective I feel in my life!

content.label: I have a lot of these style of apps on my phone and iPad and Apple Watch, by far ‘Things’ stands alone as the simplest way for me to add voice reminders and be so much more effective in achieving my goals. It’s elegant UI, it’s secure and privacy security allows me to use this very handy app across all of my devices, to feel like I have the back up memory to stay on top of errands, duties, bills that sometimes would have slipped past me. It just works for me where all the other apps I have tried to achieve this with failed to keep me engaging them. It’s so simple yet so effective. I really love this Things app and the results that I am getting in all areas of my life by utilising it.

title.label: Needs at least an online platform

content.label: Not on windows or other platforms is a hard pass no matter how good. Most companies use Windows, and people use these “to do” apps for work.

title.label: It’s great but wish it synced to google calendar

content.label: Love things 3 really has changed my productivity but wish it could sync to google calendar!
Has all the functionality I need, particularly like being able to email tasks to inbox and the deadline feature. Would really like it if I could collapse fields, otherwise excellent

Best organisational app ever! Never been so in control of my life and all the stuff I have to do everyday. You can set up daily, monthly, annual reminders and repeat them as often as you’d like. 

And the best part, this app has a logbook that saves all the stuff you’ve done, appointments you’ve attended…all of it! 

A bit of getting used to but now, an essential part of my life. 

I could not live without it now. Thank you Things!!

Things on face value, appears to be a very basic app. But as you begin to use the app more, you start to realise the sophistication, design and simplicity make this a killer app. 

Wishlist- a web app so I can use it at work (PC), the ability to have todays tasks be above projects when in area and widgets to be more reliable on iOS (they show things that you have completed as unfinished).

Being able to have a due date for sub tasks would be ideal. Is it possible? For example: an assignment date is set for a class. The sub tasks involve a due date for marking and a due date for assignment returns.

title.label: Great app and developer customer service

content.label: Thanks

This app is expensive and not as useful as Todoist. The killer feature of Todoist is that it runs everywhere, including Windows and in the browser. This is critical when you need to quickly get a thought out of your head and into the list.

On my work PC I use the browser app because I don’t want to install anything personal. On my home PC I have the Windows app and it’s a quick global shortcut to open up a dialog to add a task, no matter what application I’m in. And of course there’s the iOS, iPadOS and Apple Watch apps when those are convenient. 

The other thing is that Todoist has a free tier which still covers basically everything I need, ad-free. Things is pricey. Buying it once isn’t too bad, but then you want it on another device, and another, and my wife wants to install it, etc. And in the end you’re paying a small fortune. Take a look at how expensive it is on Mac and convince yourself that either it’s worth it or that you’re comfortable just always having to reach for your phone or iPad every time you want to note something in the list, where it’s more difficult to type and paste links etc.
Good design, simple UX, yet has everything just how I wanted.

title.label: The best to-do app in the world.

content.label:
I just wanted to commend the team for creating by far the best app on the store. 
Love all the attention to detail, and utilising any of the new iOS update features on day 1. 
You can tell the people behind Things truly care about their work. Thank you!

I use the Things iPhone/Watch app and Mac software to stay organised and it's by far the best to-do list program I've found 🙂 It has plenty of features like tags and repeating events, but has a clean easy to use design at the same time. Dark mode is beautiful, I love the filtering by tags (especially the interface on the Mac app), and being able to quickly add a task on my Mac using a keyboard shortcut is really useful. 

It's almost perfect but I would love if:
- You could collapse headings.
- You could set location-based reminders (and/or other smart reminders, like weather-based).
- You could choose a few lists that can be viewed on the Watch app, not just the today view. For example I have a weekly and monthly task list that I'd love to be able to view on my Watch! 

Overall though a great to-do app, suggestions are just me being nit-picky haha

Decided to finally upgrade. Followed links and without notification or warning downloaded the iPhone app - when I was using the iPad app previously. 
Completely useless and waste of money - Things want me to pay 2x as much for the iPad app. On top of the $15.99 for the iPhone app I do not want. There is no way to cancel the unwanted and automatically downloaded iPhone version.  
If this is your business model then you have deliberately misleading practices.

After years of relying solely on the stock reminders, things 3 can come as a nice refresher for what a to do app can do and look like. What things does better than reminders for me: more granular time settings, there’s no “deadline” and “someday” in reminders. The ability to create to dos through email can also come in handy. 

It is a bit more complicated to set up recurring events, having to tap the three dots at bottom and finish the setup before exiting a new to do in order to avoid duplicates. Also, not complaining but not a power user and I would never pay thrice for the exact same app just to be able to use cross device. Wish this app continue to stay true to the non-subscription pricing model.

title.label: Love it but can’t use on work pc

content.label: Love it but can’t use on work pc

title.label: Have to pay twice? No thanks

content.label: Have been using things on my iPhone for a while, thought i might start using it for uni stuff on my iPad but no... That's an extra $30! What a joke

title.label: This would be a great platform

content.label: The app is great, it is the best on the market. However, I use Linux and Windows for work and it would be great if I could sync with any of that platform or at least with web.

I downloaded all three versions of the app and I am loving it so far. I do hope, however, that the creators make one improvement soon. 
It would be really nice if there was an option to change the font size to suit the user’s preference. The iPad and iPhone version of the app uses a font size that is way too large in my opinion. I love the app so far, and so this is just a review with the hope that this small but helpful change can be made.

I’ve used loads of personal organisers and to-do lists and Things is the easiest to get started with and then to expand how you use it. Use it on your iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch. Tell Siri to add items when you think of them. Easy peasy!
